newsitem.title: USA: First Union denies major acquisition looms.
newsitem.headline: First Union denies major acquisition looms.

text.p: The chief executive officer of First Union Corp denied Wall Street speculation that the banking company planned to make a major acquisition to expand outside its 13-state eastern region.

"We aren't interested in a big leapfrog. We would not go to the Midwest or Southwest just because somebody (another banking company) said they're available," CEO Ed Crutchfield said in a presentation to the Atlanta Rotary Club.
Afterwards, in an interview with Reuters, Crutchfield was asked how long acquisitions would be on hold. He said: "Nothing's foreseen in the next couple of years."
Crutchfield said his plan could change if the economy went into deep recession, forcing weaker banks to sell out at cheap prices, but "our strategic direction is not going that way."
